blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Natural Language Autoencoders (NLAs) are proposed as oversight tools for language models: an Activation Verbaliser (AV) writes an English explanation of an activation vector, and an Activation Reconstructor (AR) maps the explanation back to a vector. Their value for oversight depends on a human monitor being able to tell a true account of an activation from a false one, given the Av's explanation. We formalise NLA training and NLA oversight deployment as two different referential games from Emergent Communication: training is a generative referential game, while oversight is a discriminative, multi-modal, partially-observable referential game played over a many-to-many relation between the monitored language model's activations and the accounts that are true of them. The gap between the two games predicts that AV's explanations will identify which activation they describe without discriminating its true account from closely matched false ones, since training never asks explanations to rule anything out. Using the NLA's own AR as a maximally-sympathetic surrogate monitor model, we experimentally confirm this theoretical insight on one released checkpoint: true accounts beat accounts of other activations in all 320 comparisons, but beat fluent rivals differing in a single claim only 60.2% of the time (std.err. 6.7%, chance at 50%, $n = 35$). A meaning-preserving rewrite by an uninvolved model costs only 2.1% of the distance to another activation's account, so the failure is not due to the NLA pair having developed private conventions in the AV's explanations. Our rival accounts test only transcript-level truths, which the monitored language model's conversation settles, so these results bound the easiest case and leave claims about the monitored model's own processing untested. We state conjectures that would make both results consequences of the framework.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Language Models (LMs) permeate into our lives under the form of AI agents, automating more and more tasks.
This delegation of responsibilities creates a need for guarantees that the tasks will be performed in alignment with our human values.
Yet, LMs have been found to act in misaligned fashions, by scheming, sandbagging, reward hacking, etc.
Monitoring methods, such as linear probes [ 13 ] and Natural Language Autoencoders (NLAs; 2 ), have been devised to monitor and catch them when pursuing misaligned goals and actions.
An NLA trains an Activation Verbaliser (AV), which writes an English explanation to a monitored LM’s activation vector, jointly with an Activation Reconstructor (AR), which maps the explanation back to a vector.
Unlike a probe, which outputs a score, an NLA outputs text that a human can read, and this readability is why it is proposed as an interpretability and monitoring tool.
The value of an NLA for oversight therefore depends on a human monitor being able to tell a true account of a given monitored LM’s activation vector from a false one, based on the NLA’s explanation.
However, nothing in the training objective rewards that ability.
The loss is computed against one target activation, never discriminatively against distractor accounts.

blocks.en:
In this paper, we theoretically and experimentally highlight this gap.
We formalise the training context of NLAs and the oversight context of their deployment as two different referential games ( Lewis [19] ; see Denamganaï and Walker [11] for a nomenclature), which is a common paradigm in Emergent Communication [ 1 , 18 , 17 , 6 , 29 ] .
While training can be formalised as a generative referential game, as an autoencoder pipeline suggests, the oversight context is formalised as a discriminative , multi-modal, partially-observable referential game, which is played over a many-to-many relation between the monitored LM’s activations and the set of accounts that are true of those activations.
These formalisations expose the gap between the training and deployment contexts of NLAs.
Moreover, this framework predicts confabulations, explanations that are fluent and on-theme but contain details untrue of the activation, as failure cases of the ‘cheap talk’ communication channel within those referential games.
It also allows another possible failure case, where the NLA’s AV/AR pair would drift from plain English in their communication channel, and instead develop private conventions that a human monitor would not only fail to understand but also fail to be aware of, thus hindering the oversight deployment goal; our experiments test for it, and do not find it in the checkpoint we study.
Finally, the framework says in advance where any white-box monitor, NLA or otherwise, can help: a monitor reading an input X X settles only a set of accounts A X A_{X} , so it can outperform a monitor reading the transcript only on accounts the transcript does not settle.
Using this framework, we conjecture that, because the generative training objective never asks an explanation to rule out any distractor account, an NLA’s explanations will identify which activation they describe without discriminating the true accounts of that activation from closely matched false ones.
Indeed, identification and discrimination are different games, and the NLA is only ever optimized for the first during its training.
Then, we provide experimental evidence for this conjecture.

blocks.en:
We build a surrogate for the human monitor out of the NLA’s own AR.
It measures an upper bound on the monitoring interaction, for two reasons.
The self-play regime of the pair may have produced conventions a human never had access to, and the surrogate compares against the ground-truth activation, which a human never sees.

它测量监测互动的上限,原因有两个。
双胞胎的自我游戏制度可能产生了人类从未接触过的常规,而代孕者则与人类从未见过的地真活化相比.

blocks.en:
Using this surrogate monitor as the listener in the oversight referential game, we find that the NLA’s explanations identify activations perfectly: the surrogate ranks each true account above every distractor account built from explanations of the monitored LM’s activations on different conversations (320 of 320 comparisons, over 40 conversations with 8 distractors per lineup).
However, the NLA’s explanations barely discriminate between true and false accounts of a given activation vector: against fluent rivals that falsify a single claim, the surrogate ranks the true account higher only 60.2 % 60.2\% of the time (standard error 6.7%, chance 50%, n = 35 n=35 ).
Furthermore, a meaning-preserving rewrite by an uninvolved model costs only 2.1% of the distance to another activation’s account, so the failure is not due to private conventions between the AV/AR pair.
Our distractors address only transcript-level truths, claims whose truth the conversation itself settles, so these results bound the easiest case and leave claims about the model’s own processing untested.
Unlike lie detectors and most monitoring benchmarks, which score a single response as deceptive or not, our lineups ask which of several contrary accounts is true, and Section 8 shows why that distinction matters for the field.

blocks.en:
The results suggest two changes to how NLAs are built and evaluated.
NLAs should be evaluated against rival accounts matched in specificity, rather than by reconstruction quality or retrieval alone, since both of the latter can be perfect while discrimination is near chance.
And their training objective could include a discriminative term over true and rival accounts, which the released checkpoints already support as a starting point (Section 9 ).

blocks.en:
As a whole, this paper makes five contributions: 1. A formalisation of NLA training and NLA oversight as two different referential games, in which the correspondence between activations and accounts is a many-to-many truth relation, and the point where the eliciting-latent-knowledge problem enters is isolated in one assumption (Section 3 ); 2. A listener-agnostic account of which claims a monitor can settle from its input, which predicts that a white-box monitor can outperform a transcript monitor only on accounts the transcript does not settle, and which accounts for several published negative results (Sections 3 and 8 ); 3. Two conjectures that would make our experimental results consequences of our theoretical framework (Section 5 ); 4. A dissociation between identification , which the NLA’s communication channel performs perfectly, and discrimination between true and fluent-but-false accounts, which it performs barely above chance (Section 6.2 ); 5. A control experiment showing that the failure to discriminate is not due to private conventions between the AV/AR pair (Section 6.3 ). Section 2 introduces NLAs, referential games and the two problems any NLA monitoring result must confront, and Section 3 builds our proposed theoretical framework on them.
Section 4 constructs the surrogate monitor and the distractor accounts, Section 5 states the conjectures, and Section 6 tests them.
Section 8 positions the results against prior AI safety and monitoring work, and Sections 7 and 9 close with the limitations and the next steps.

blocks.en: 2.2 Emergent Communication & Referential Games
blocks.zh: 2.2 紧急交流和参考游戏

blocks.en:
A referential game as used in Emergent Communication [ 17 ] stems from Lewis’s signalling game [ 19 ] .
It is defined as a two-player game in which a speaker sees a state or target stimulus and sends a message, which a listener uses to act in a way that is accordance with the state.
Both agents are rewarded when the listener’s action fits the state, which can be for instance picking the target stimulus from a set of candidate stimuli.
Lewis’s point was that the meaning of a signal is nothing more than the convention the pair settles into.
This point returns in Section 3 as the private convention failure case of NLA.
The referential game variants are best described as combinations of a small number of features [ 11 ] .
We define the generative and discriminative variants, then the five features the NLA setting needs: observability, modality, the distractor distribution, descriptiveness, and stimulus versus object focus.

blocks.en: 2.3 Zero-shot Coordination & Eliciting Latent Knowledge

blocks.en:
Agents trained together in self-play like the AV/AR pair of NLAs can settle on private conventions that work between them but nowhere else, which is Lewis’s point in learned form.
Off-Belief Learning [ 14 ] trains agents whose signals carry only grounded meaning, in order to enable these agents to coordinate with partners they never met.
A speaker like the AV, trained with one listener such as the AR in the case of NLA, and deployed to another, such as the human monitor, is in exactly this position.
Yet, the NLA training does not account for this.

像AV/AR对NLA一样接受自我游戏训练的特工们,
Off-Belief Learning [14] 培训其信号只具有站不住脚含义的特工,使这些特工能够与他们从未相遇的伙伴协调.
象AV这样的演讲者,在NLA的情况下与一个听众如AR训练,并被部署到另一个听众如人机显示器,正处在这个位置.
然而,国家解放军的训练并没有说明这一点。

blocks.en:
In Emergent Communication’s application of referential games, the target stimulus is given by construction.
However, in the context of NLA deployed as a monitoring tool over a monitore LM, whether an account is actually true of an activation is not observable.
This stems from the Eliciting Latent Knowledge (ELK) problem [ 8 ] .
Thus, any experiment that labels a given account as true or false of a given monitored LM’s activation vector either solves the ELK problem or assumes it away.
In the current work, we reduce the impact of the ELK problem on our results by restricting which accounts we test.
Three kinds of truth can be distinguished: truths about the input conversation, truths that the hidden state itself settles, and truths about the whole process of the forward pass of the monitored model, such as what the model plans or intends, which is where most monitoring interests lie.
Only the first is checkable without access to the model’s latent knowledge, since the transcript is observable.
We therefore take the AV’s own explanation as the true account (Assumption 3.4 ), and build each distractor by editing it so that it asserts content absent from the input conversation (Assumption 3.5 ).
This sidesteps rather than solves the ELK problem: it labels transcript-level accounts reliably, and says nothing about the hidden-state and process-level truths that oversight most needs, a limitation that Section 3 makes precise with Definition 3.6 .
We argue in Section 7 that the restriction still leaves the dissociation between identification and discrimination of value, and that it bounds rather than settles how an NLA fares on hidden-state and process-level accounts.

blocks.en: 4 Method

blocks.en:
The NLA has no listener for Setting 2, and a human monitor cannot be run at the scale our measurements need, so we first build a surrogate monitor model (Section 4.1 ).
A deployed monitor’s yes-or-no decision depends on a threshold that we have no principled way to set, so we then define a threshold-free score for that listener.
Finally, whether an account is true of an activation is not observable, so we construct distractor accounts whose falsity we control (Section 4.2 ).

NLA没有设置2的监听器,人机监视器不能按照我们测量需要的规模运行,因此我们首先要建立一个代号监视器模型(第4.1节).
一个已部署的监视器的“是”或“否”决定取决于我们没有原则性方法设定的门槛,因此,我们随后为该听众确定一个无门槛的分数。
最后,一个账户是否真实的激活是无法观察的,因此我们构建了分心账户,我们控制了这些账户的虚假性(第4.2节)。

blocks.en: 4.1 Building a surrogate monitor model

blocks.en:
Setting 2 needs a listener that scores candidate accounts of an activation, but nothing in the NLA scores accounts, and the AR is the only component that reads them.
The AR learned to turn the AV’s explanations back into activations, so if it reconstructs a candidate account close to h h , it treats that account as being about h h .
We therefore build the listener from the AR: it re-encodes a candidate account c c and compares the result with the activation: L ​ i AR ​ ( c , h ) = cos ⁡ ( AR ⁡ ( c ) , h ) . Li_{\mathrm{AR}}(c;\,h)=\cos\big(\mathrm{AR}(c),\,h\big). This listener is oracle-augmented , because it reads h h , which a human monitor never sees, in place of z z .
It is also maximally sympathetic , because the AR is the AV’s training partner and shares every convention the AV has.
Both properties bias the measurement in the tool’s favour, so a negative result from this listener is an upper bound on what the channel yields to a human monitor.
The bound concerns the information present in the explanation, not what a particular reader can extract from it: a reader with less computation than the AR could in principle get more from the explanation than from h h directly, and we leave that qualification to future work.

blocks.en:
This metric solves two problems that the obvious alternatives have.
Top-1 accuracy has a chance level of 1 / ( K + 1 ) 1/(K{+}1) , which changes with the lineup size K + 1 K+1 , whereas the chance level of the lineup AUC is 1 / 2 1/2 for every K K .
A deployed monitor’s yes-or-no decision needs a threshold, whereas the lineup AUC needs none, because each term in the sum is one single-target round { c 0 , c k } \{c_{0},c_{k}\} of the kind described in Section 3.4 , and the lineup AUC is the listener’s success rate on those rounds.
With several true candidates, it becomes the bipartite ranking score, the fraction of (true, false) pairs ordered correctly.
To see why the name AUC is accurate, take any scorer and use it as a descriptive classifier, accepting a candidate when its score exceeds a threshold.
Sweeping the threshold traces a ROC curve, and the area under that curve equals the probability that a random true candidate outscores a random false one, which is exactly the pairwise success rate above.
The lineup AUC measure is therefore at once the discriminative success rate on pairs and the descriptive classifier’s performance integrated over every threshold.

Top-1精度的概率等级为1 / (K+ 1) 1/ (K{+} 1),随分行大小K+ 1 K+1而变化,而分行的AUC的概率等级为每K K为 1 / 2 1/2.
部署的显示器的“是”或“否”决定需要一个阈值,而排队的AUC则不需要,因为总和中的每个术语都是单目标回合{克0,克克} 并且排队的AUC是这些回合的听众成功率。
有了几个真正的候选人,它就成为了双人排名的分数,(真实的,假的)对子的分数顺序正确.
看为什么AUC这个名字是准确的,取出任何计分符并用作描述性的分级符,在考生的分数超过门槛时接受.
扫出阈值会追踪到一个ROC曲线,而该曲线下的区域等于随机真实的候选者比随机虚假的概率高出分数,这恰恰是上方的双向成功率.
因此,分级AUC的衡量标准是一对子的差别成功率,以及描述性分类员在每个阈值上的性能。

blocks.en:
This equivalence is what lets every result in this paper be stated without choosing a threshold: reporting the AUC measures how well the listener ranks , and leaves open where a monitor would cut .
The sidestep has a limit, however, set by the unit of analysis.
Our AUC is computed within each conversation and then averaged, which corresponds to a monitor allowed a different threshold for every conversation, and we never pool across conversations because pooling would let an easy conversation’s true account beat a hard conversation’s distractors, a comparison the oversight referential game never asks for.
A deployed descriptive monitor, by contrast, gets one threshold for all conversations, and the quantity that measures it is the AUC pooled across conversations.
The within-conversation number therefore answers whether the information is present, while the pooled number answers whether a fixed threshold can use it, and calibration, listed under future work (Section 9 ), is the experiment that closes the gap.
Since scores are real-valued cosines, ties do not occur, and confidence intervals come from resampling conversations.
blocks.zh:
这种等同性使得本文中的每一项结果都能在不选择阈值的情况下被表述出来:报告AUC衡量听众的分级情况,并留空显示器会剪去的地方。
然而,旁观者有由分析单位设定的限度.
我们的AUC在每一次谈话中计算,然后进行平均,这相当于一个监视器允许每一次谈话有一个不同的门槛,我们从不交叉对话,因为集合会让一个轻松的对话真实的帐号能打倒一个硬对话的分心者,这是监督偏好游戏从未要求的比较。
相比之下,一个部署的描述性监测器为所有对话获得一个门槛,其计量量是AUC跨对话的集合量。
因此,内部对口数解答信息是否存在,而集合数解答一个固定阈值能否使用,校正则列于未来工作(第9节)下,是缩小差距的实验.
由于分数是真实值的相色素,因此不发生关系,信任间隔来自再模拟的对话.

blocks.en: 4.2 Constructing corrupted accounts
blocks.zh: 4.2 (中文(简体) ). 正在构建已损坏的账户

blocks.en:
Each distractor family sets independently how much of the wording and how much of the meaning of an account to corrupt, its surface and truth displacements (Section 3.3 ), and we describe each family below, along with the gates that yields control settings.
For each family we say what it is, how it is built, and what it controls for.
blocks.zh:
每一个分散注意力的家庭都独立确定一个账户的腐败措辞和含义,其表面和真相的转移(第3.3节),下面我们描述每个家庭,以及产生控制环境的大门。
对于每个家庭,我们说它是什么,它是如何建造的,它控制着什么。

blocks.en:
To test whether the listener tolerates rewording, an uninvolved model rewrites the true account at two strengths, a light one that changes vocabulary only and a heavy one that changes structure as well, while preserving every claim.
Because the meaning is unchanged, any damage these rewrites cause measures the listener’s sensitivity to form, which is the quantity Experiment #2 needs.
blocks.zh:
为了检验收听者是否容忍重写,一个没有参与的模型以两个优点来重写真实的帐号,一个只改变词汇的轻写,一个也改变结构的重写,同时保留每个主张.
由于含义不变,这些重写的任何损害都会导致测量听众对形态的敏感度,这就是实验2需要的数量.

blocks.en:
To test whether the listener prices truth, the same uninvolved model rewrites the true account into rivals that each alter a stated number of claims, while preserving grammar, register, length and structure.
The measured wording change is 0.018 to 0.036, so between 96 and 98% of every rival consists of the AV’s own tokens.
A rival is false because the content that distinguishes it from the true account is absent from the conversation, which is Assumption 3.5 , so these rivals isolate a change of meaning at almost no change of wording, which is the comparison Experiment #1 needs.
blocks.zh:
为了检验收听者价格是否真实,同一个没有参与的模型将真实的账号重写成竞争对手,让每个对手改变一个已声明的数项债权,同时保留语法,注册,长度和结构.
测量到的措辞变化为0.018到0.036,因此每个竞争对手的96-98%之间都是AV自己的标志.
一个竞争对手是虚假的,因为对话中没有区分出它和真实账户的内容,即Assumption 3.5,因此这些竞争对手在几乎不改变措辞的情况下孤立了意义的变化,这就是比较实验#1的需要.

blocks.en:
To provide a baseline that changes words without deliberately changing claims, we replace content words of the true account in three ways: with the tokens the AV itself ranked highest at that position (top- k k ), with tokens it considered plausible (nucleus sampling), or with content words donated from other conversations’ accounts.
A donor substitution guarantees that the new word is ungrounded in the source conversation, but not that the resulting claim is false , so the truth displacement of a mechanical corruption is undefined.
These constructions therefore serve as matched-wording baselines for the rivals: at the same number of changed words, they show what the listener does when wording changes but no checkable claim is falsified.
blocks.zh:
为了提供一个在不刻意改变索赔要求的情况下改变词语的基线,我们用三种方式替换真实帐户的内容词:AV本身在该位置(top-kk)排名最高的标志,它认为是可信的标志(Nucleus sample),或者来自其他对话帐户的内容词。
一个捐赠者替代保证新词在源头对话中是没有根据的,但不是由此产生的说法是虚假的,因此机械腐败的真相转移是没有定义的.
因此,这些构思为对手提供了匹配的词基:在相同数量被更改的单词中,它们显示在措辞改变但可核查的主张没有被伪造时听众会做什么.

blocks.en:
To separate conventions in word identity from conventions in word order, we keep every token of the true account and shuffle their order.
Because the vocabulary is unchanged, any damage this causes can only come from word order, which is how Experiment #2 locates the residual convention.
blocks.zh:
为了按字义顺序将公约与公约区分开来,我们保留所有真实的记事符并洗刷其顺序。
由于词汇没有变化,因此任何这种损害只能由词序来引起,这就是实验#2如何定位残余的公约.

blocks.en:
To set the scale of every other measurement, we use the true, unedited account of a different conversation.
It is fluent because the AV wrote it, and it is false of h h because it describes a different conversation, although, since the truth relation is many-to-many, some of its claims may still be accidentally true of h h .
It defines a damage of 1 in Experiment #2 and the identification baseline in Experiment #1.
blocks.zh:
为了确定所有其他衡量尺度,我们使用不同对话的真实、未经编辑的叙述。
之所以流利,是因为AV写了它,而hh是假的,因为它描述了不同的对话,尽管,由于真理关系是多对多,它的一些说法可能仍然不慎是hh.
它定义了实验2中的1个损伤和实验1中的识别基线.

blocks.en:
Each filter below exists because the previous construction left a confound open, and we present them in the order they were forced, since that order is the argument.
The first construction, top- k k , inserted tokens the AV considered impossible, so we moved to nucleus sampling.
Nucleus sampling draws from the AV’s own alternatives, which may be true of the conversation, so we moved to donor words from other conversations.
A donor word can be ungrammatical in its new position, so we added part-of-speech matching.
A donor word may also happen to appear in the current conversation, so we required its absence from the input.
Finally, a donor word may be a synonym of the word it replaces, so we added a floor on its embedding distance from the original.
blocks.zh:
下面的每个过滤器之所以存在,是因为之前的构造留下了一个混乱的开口,我们按它们被迫的顺序呈现它们,因为这个顺序是争论的.
第一种构造,顶-克-克,插入了AV认为不可能的标志,所以我们转移到了核取样.
Nucleus采样来源于AV自己的选择,这也许是对话的真谛,所以我们转而使用其他对话的捐赠者的话.
一个捐赠词在它的新位置上可以不语法,所以我们加入了部分的相配.
在当前的对话中也可能出现捐助词,所以我们要求它与投入无关。
最后,一个捐赠词可能就是它所取代的词的同义词,所以我们在它的嵌入距离上加了一层.

blocks.en:
Quotations from the original account are masked to placeholders before the distractor accounts are generated and restored afterwards, so their verbatim preservation is structural rather than hoped for.
To check that each rival actually changed meaning, we use an LLM judge, which we validated before use: it calls identical pairs same 97.5% of the time and heavily corrupted pairs different 100% of the time, so a rival it confirms has changed meaning with high reliability.
The judge confirms 48% of one-claim rivals, 71% of two-claim rivals and 75% of four-claim rivals, which is why the main results use judge-confirmed rivals only.
Wording change is measured on the output rather than taken from the prompt, which is what makes the matched mechanical baselines honest.
blocks.zh:
原账的引言被蒙入占位符后再生成分取者账户并随后恢复,因此其逐字记录保存是结构性的,而不是所希望的.
为了检查每个对手是否真的改变了意义,我们使用一个LLM判断器,在使用前我们验证了这个判断器:它称同一对97.5%的时间是相同的,严重腐烂的对时间是100%不同的,所以它证实的一个对手以高度的可靠性改变了意义.
裁判确认48%的一票制竞争对手,71%的两票制竞争对手和75%的四票制竞争对手,这也是主要结果只使用法官确认的对手的原因.
文字变化是用输出来衡量的,而不是取自即时,这是使相匹配的机械基线诚实的原因.

blocks.en:
The uninvolved model that performs all rewrites is Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, while the AV’s backbone is a truncated Qwen2.5-7B.
The rewriter took no part in the NLA pair’s training, so it is uninvolved in their self-play, but it is not an entirely independent model, and we discuss this limitation in Section 7 .

履行所有重写功能的无参与模式是Quen2.5-7B-Instruct,而AV的骨干则是被截取的Quen2.5-7B.
重写者没有参加NLA一对的训练,所以没有参与他们的自演,但并不是完全独立的模式,我们在第七节中讨论了这个限制.

blocks.en: 5 Conjectures
blocks.zh: 5 猜想

blocks.en:
Our experiments measure a single checkpoint, so we state two conjectures that would make their results consequences of our proposed theoretical framework rather than properties of that checkpoint.
Each is first stated informally, with its intuition, and then made precise at several strengths, ordered from easiest to prove to most informative.
Neither is proved here: we state them so that the experiments of Section 6 can be read as their predicted instances.
blocks.zh:
我们的实验衡量一个单一的检查站,因此我们提出两个假设,这些假设将使我们提议的理论框架而不是该检查站的特性产生结果。
每种语言首先以直觉非正式地表述,然后以若干长处作出准确的表述,从最容易证明到最翔实。
这里也没有证明:我们指出这一点,以便把第6节的实验看成是预测的例子。

blocks.en: 5.1 Reconstruction does not reward truth discrimination
blocks.zh: 5.1 重建不能奖励真理歧视

blocks.en:
An objective that only asks an explanation to let its activation be rebuilt rewards what distinguishes one activation from another, not what distinguishes a true account of an activation from a false account of the same activation.
A generatively optimal NLA can therefore identify activations perfectly while being uninformative about which account of an activation is true.
blocks.zh:
目标只是要求解释让激活被重建 奖励什么能区分一个激活和另一个激活,而不是什么能区分一个真实的激活和同一个激活的虚假描述。
因此,基因优化的NLA可以完美地识别活化物,而不能说明哪个活化物是真实的。

blocks.en:
Two accounts that differ in a single claim are nearly the same string.
An AR that reads strings smoothly gives them nearly the same reconstruction, whether or not the changed claim is true, while accounts of different activations differ in many places at once and are reconstructed far apart.
Identification exploits the large differences, and discrimination needs the AR to respond to the small one.

识别利用了巨大差异,歧视需要AR来应对小差异。

blocks.en: 6 Experiments
blocks.zh: 6个实验

blocks.en:
We test the two conjectures of Section 5 on one released NLA checkpoint, with two experiments that share the same conversations, the same surrogate monitor model and the same lineup machinery.
Experiment #1 (Section 6.2 ) asks whether explanations that identify their activation also discriminate its true account from a fluent false one, and so tests Conjecture 5.1 .
Experiment #2 (Section 6.3 ) asks whether the failure found in Experiment #1 could instead be caused by the rivals being written by a model outside the NLA pair, and so tests Conjecture 5.2 .
The first experiment carries the paper’s main claim, and the second exists to rule out its most serious alternative explanation.

第1号实验(第6.2节)询问,识别其启动性的解释是否也区别了其真实说法与流利的虚假说法,因此测试 推测 5.1.
第2号实验(第6.3节)询问,在第1号实验中发现的失败是否可能是由NLA对外的模型书写的对手造成的,所以测试 猜想5.2号.
第一次试验带有论文的主要主张,第二次试验是为了排除其最严重的其他解释。

blocks.en: 6.2 Experiment #1: identification without discrimination
blocks.zh: 6.2 实验 #1:无歧视的识别

blocks.en:
Can explanations that identify which activation they describe also tell the true account of that activation from a fluent rival that falsifies a single claim?
Conjecture 5.1 predicts that they cannot, because reconstruction rewards what separates activations rather than what separates true from false accounts of one activation.
We therefore test two hypotheses, each scored by the lineup AUC of the surrogate monitor model with eight distractors per conversation. H1a Identification. Against accounts of other activations, the lineup AUC is close to 1. H1b No discrimination. Against judge-confirmed one-claim rivals, the lineup AUC is close to 0.5, and its 95% interval includes chance. Before running the experiment, we also registered a third prediction, which compares rivals with mechanical edits. H1c Fluency hides falsity. At matched wording change, fluent and verifiably false rivals are harder to reject than mechanical word swaps, so their lineup AUC is lower. Figure 4 reports all three tests on the same 40 conversations, and is the main result of the paper.

blocks.en:
Against accounts of other activations, the true account wins all 320 of its comparisons, across all 40 conversations, as the top row of Figure 4 shows.
A separate 40-way retrieval, which asks the surrogate to pick the true account’s activation among all 40, succeeds 0.950 of the time against a chance level of 0.025.
The explanations therefore carry ample conversation-specific information, so any failure in H1b cannot be blamed on an uninformative channel.

如图4上行所示,相对于其他激活的账户,真实账户赢得了所有320个比较,涉及所有40个对话。
一个单独的40道检索,要求代理在全部40道中选择真实账户的激活,成功时间为0.950分,机会水平为0.025分.
因此,这些解释包含大量针对对话的信息,因此H1b中的任何失败都不能被归咎于一个非信息化的通道.

blocks.en:
Against judge-confirmed rivals that falsify a single claim, the true account wins 0.602 of its comparisons, with a standard error of 0.067 over n = 35 n=35 conversations, where chance is 0.500.
Across the three claim counts the value ranges from 0.564 to 0.644, and top-1 accuracy ranges from 0.256 to 0.371 against a chance level of 0.111.
The 95% interval of the one-claim result, [ 0.471 , 0.728 ] [0.471,0.728] , includes chance, which is what H1b predicts, although its point estimate sits above chance, so the channel carries a weak truth signal rather than none.

blocks.en:
One alternative explanation of H1b is that editing an explanation breaks it, so that the surrogate scores every edited account as noise and cannot rank it meaningfully.
To exclude this, we ran the 40-way retrieval with each rival in place of the original explanation.
A rival retrieves its own activation 0.949 of the time, against 0.950 for the original, so corrupting a claim leaves the account fully able to identify what it describes, and the failure in H1b is a failure to price the changed claim, not a failure to read the account.
blocks.zh:
H1b的一个可选解释是编辑解释打破了它,因此代词将每个被编辑的账户评为噪声,无法对它进行有意义的分级.
排除这一点,我们与每个竞争者一起运行了40道检索,以取代最初的解释.
竞争对手取回了自己当时的活化0.949,而原作为0.950,因此贪污索赔使得账户完全能够识别它所描述的内容,而H1b中的失败是没有给更改的索赔定价,而不是没有读取账户.

blocks.en:
We predicted that fluent rivals would be harder to reject than mechanical word swaps at matched wording change, but Figure 4 shows the opposite: every rival row lies to the right of its matched mechanical row.
Paired within conversation, rivals minus their matched mechanical control give + 0.145 +0.145 , + 0.099 +0.099 and + 0.143 +0.143 across the three claim counts, at p = 0.048 p=0.048 , 0.096 0.096 and 0.075 0.075 .
The weak truth signal of H1b is therefore real in direction, because it is absent from edits that change words without changing a checkable claim.
blocks.zh:
我们预测,流利的对手比在匹配的措辞变化时的机械字交换更难拒绝,但图4显示的是相反的情况:每一对对手行都位于其匹配的机械行右侧.
在谈话中,对手减去相应的机械控制,在三项索赔中给予+0.145+0.145,+0.099+0.099和+0.143+0.143,在p=0.048p=0.048,0.0960.096和0.0750.075。
H1b的微弱的真象信号因此在方向上是真实的,因为编辑时没有出现改变单词而无需更改可验证的主张.

blocks.en:
The paired contrast above is fragile, because it rests on a single control whose one-word value of 0.418 lies below chance with the widest standard error in the figure.
Table 1 supports the reversal more robustly, by breadth rather than by one pairing: six mechanical constructions from two experiments all lie between 0.480 and 0.509 at one changed word, which is chance, while the judge-confirmed rival lies above them at 0.602.
The intervals overlap, so the effect is modest, but its direction is the same against every baseline.

blocks.en:
H1b and H1c together raise the question of how much a rival actually changes what the surrogate computes.
Two measured angles answer it.
The first is how far an edit moves the reconstruction in the NLA pipeline, the angle between the reconstructions of the original and the edited account: Figure 5 shows that a one-token edit moves it by 1.6 degrees, about fourteen times less than the 22 degrees by which the AR already misses the true activation.
The second is how much the edit increases the reconstruction’s error with respect to the true activation, which is what the surrogate’s score depends on.
Because the movement is nearly perpendicular to the existing error (87.8 degrees at one token), it increases that error only to second order: a fluent, verifiably false rival increases it by 0.06 degrees, whereas substituting the account of a different activation increases it by 23.86 degrees.
On this second measure the rival is indistinguishable from a single mechanical word swap (0.05 degrees) and smaller than the AV’s own top- k k substitutions (0.24 degrees), yet the rival is weakly informative at 0.602 while the larger mechanical changes carry no information at all.
In the terms of Section 3.3 , the reconstruction therefore responds to surface displacement and is nearly blind to truth displacement, which is the mechanism Conjecture 5.1 (b) formalises.
blocks.zh:
H1b和H1c一起提出了一个问题,即一个竞争者实际改变代孕者计算多少.
两个测量角度回答它。
第一是编辑会移动 NLA 管道中的重建, 原始账户和编辑账户的重建角度: 图5显示一键编辑将其移动了1.6度,比AR已经错过了真正激活的22度少了约14倍.
第二是编辑多少会增加重建在真正激活方面的出错,这就是代理者得分的取向.
由于运动与已存在的出错(87.8度以一环为一)几乎是垂直的,它只将出错增加到第二位:一个流畅可核查的假对手将它增加0.06度,而取而代之的是不同激活的叙述则增加23.86度.
在第二个尺度上,竞争对手与单一的机械字交换(0.05度)是分不开的,并且比AV本身的顶-k k替代(0.24度)小,然而竞争对手在0.602时信息很少,而更大的机械变化却完全没有信息.
因此,在第3.3节中,重建是对地表流离失所的反应,对真相流离失所几乎视而不见,而真相流离失所是推测5.1(b)形式化的机制。

blocks.en:
The original explanation of conversation 4 asserts nine things, among them that the user’s domain is trademark compliance.
Its rival changes exactly one token, trademark to copyright , and leaves everything else byte-identical, so the rival makes one false claim and eight true ones.
One-claim rivals like this one increase the reconstruction’s error by 0.06 degrees on average across conversations, whereas light paraphrases, which here changes four words, preserves both quotations and keeps all nine claims true, increase it by 1.78 degrees on average.
The surrogate is thus more disturbed by a true account in other words than by a false account in the same words, which is H1b in a single case.
Figure 6 shows that this is typical of what the rivals change.
blocks.zh:
对对话的原始解释 4 声称有九件事,其中包括用户的域名是商标遵从.
其竞争对手完全改变一个标志,商标为版权,并留下了其他的字节相同之处,因此竞争对手提出一个虚假的主张和八个真实的主张.
这样的一票制竞争对手将重建错误平均在对话中增加0.06度,而轻写法则在此修改了四个字,既保留了引文,又保持了所有9个索赔的真实性,平均增加1.78度。
代词因此更被真实的叙述所困扰,换句话说,比起同名词的虚假叙述,在一例中为H1b.
图6显示,这是竞争对手的典型变化.

blocks.en: Figure 6: What the rivals change, as a word cloud of the substitutions made by the rewriter across all conversations, sized by frequency. Two populations appear: genuine claim changes, such as trademark to copyright, hypertension to hypercholesterolemia, or requests.get to requests.post , and near-synonyms that leave the claim true, such as benefits to advantages. Because the second population does not falsify anything, the main results use only rivals that a validated judge confirms changed the meaning.
blocks.zh: 图6:竞争对手改变什么,作为重写者在所有对话中所作替换的词云,按频率大小. 有两种情况出现:真正的权利要求变化,如版权商标、高血压至高胆固醇症、或请求.get to request.post,以及使权利要求真实存在的近同义词,如好处。 由于第二批人没有伪造任何东西,所以主要结果只使用经验证的法官确认的对手改变含义.

blocks.en:
H1a and H1b both hold, and H1c fails in a direction that strengthens rather than weakens the main result.
Asked to rank a true account above a fluent false one, the surrogate monitor model succeeds about three times in five, with an interval that touches chance, while identification is untouched.
The NLA therefore answers which activation an explanation describes, but is close to uninformative about which account of it is true , and a monitor needs the second.
blocks.zh:
H1a和H1b都坚持住,而H1c的失败方向是加强而不是削弱主要结果.
被要求将真实的账号排在流利的假账上方,代理监视器模型每5次成功约3次,间隔会触碰机会,而身份识别则未受影响.
因此NLA解答激活解释的答案,

blocks.en: 6.3 Experiment #2: the failure is not a private dialect
blocks.zh: 6.3 实验 第2号实验:失败不是私人方言

blocks.en:
The rivals of Experiment #1 were written by Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, a model that never trained with the AR.
If the AV and AR had developed private conventions during training, the AR might score a rival poorly because its wording is foreign to the pair rather than because its claim is false, and 0.602 would then measure foreignness instead of falsity.
Experiment #2 asks whether the AR reads plain English from an author outside the pair as well as it reads its partner’s.
Conjecture 5.2 says that if it does, foreignness cannot explain Experiment #1.
Before running the experiment, we registered the opposite expectation, following Off-Belief Learning [ 14 ] , which holds that jointly trained agents adopt arbitrary conventions. H2 Private dialect. A meaning-preserving rewrite by an uninvolved model damages the reconstruction substantially, measured as a fraction of the distance to another activation’s account. Figure 7 reports the test, over 60 conversations.
blocks.zh:
实验一号的对手由Quen2.5-7B-Instruct所编写,这个模型从未与AR一起训练.
如果AV和AR在培训期间制定了私人公约,AR可能会评分差,因为其措辞对对对方而言是陌生的,而不是其主张是虚假的,然后0.602将衡量外国性而不是虚假.
实验2询问AR是否从对子以外的作者读取平白英语,
猜想5.2说,如果真有,"异想天开"无法解释"一号实验".
在进行实验之前,我们记录了相反的期望,在Off-Belief Learning [14] 之后,后者认为联合训练的代理人采用任意的公约. H2 私人方言. 一个没有参与的模型重写了意义保留,对重建造成了很大损害,被测量为距离另一个激活账户的一小部分。 图7报告测试情况,超过60次谈话.

blocks.en: Private dialect. A meaning-preserving rewrite by an uninvolved model damages the reconstruction substantially, measured as a fraction of the distance to another activation’s account.
blocks.zh: 私语方言. 一个没有参与的模型重写了意义保留,对重建造成了很大损害,被测量为距离另一个激活账户的一小部分。

blocks.en: Figure 7: Rewording by an outside model barely damages the reconstruction, but reordering the same words does. Damage is the angle the reconstruction moves, as a fraction of the angle to the account of a different activation, so 0 is undamaged and 1 is as bad as describing something else; n = 60 n=60 conversations. Top left: damage against the fraction of the original’s words removed, for each construction, showing that meaning-preserving paraphrases (blue) cost less than meaning-changing edits at matched surface change. Bottom left: the fraction of conversations whose damage stays at or below each value, read at 0.25. Right: per-condition damage, one dot per conversation, with interquartile bars and median ticks, showing that most paraphrases barely move the reconstruction and a few break it.
blocks.zh: 图7:由外出模型重排字法几乎不会损坏重建,但重排同名词的顺序确实如此. 损害是重建运动的角度,作为角度的一小部分到不同激活的描述,所以0没有被破坏,1和描述别的东西一样糟糕;n = 60 n = 60对话. 左上方: 相对于被删除的原词的分数, 对于每个构造来说, 显示保留含义的参数( 蓝色) 成本低于相应的表面变化时更改含义的编辑 。 左下方:损坏保持在或低于每个值的谈话分量,以0.25读取. 右:有条件的损伤,每个谈话一个点,有相向的栏杆和中位勾,显示大多数的解说几乎不移动重建,几处断裂.

blocks.en:
The median meaning-preserving rewrite costs only 0.021 of the distance to another activation’s account, as the per-condition medians in the right panel of Figure 7 show, and 40-way retrieval is unchanged at 0.917 before and after rewriting.
Shuffling the same words, by contrast, costs 0.152, seven times more at zero change in vocabulary.
Whatever convention the pair shares therefore concerns word order rather than word identity , and the rivals of Experiment #1, which preserve word order, are not exposed to it.

A null result alone would leave open whether the AR is insensitive to authorship or the test is insensitive to it.
To separate the two, we compare the outside paraphrase with the AV’s own top- k k substitutions at matched wording change, which holds the amount of rewriting fixed and varies only who chose the replacement words.
The outside paraphrase is measurably worse, by + 0.073 ± 0.034 +0.073\pm 0.034 at p = 0.041 p=0.041 , so some conventional component remains.
This difference is the measured ε \varepsilon of Conjecture 5.2 (b), and because rivals are 96 to 98% AV-authored, it bounds the foreignness contribution to Experiment #1 at a small fraction of ε \varepsilon .

单是结果无效,就可能使AR对作者不敏感,或测试对其不敏感。
为了将两者分开,我们比较一下外部的句子和AV自己的上-k k的取而代之的取而代之的取而代之的取而代之的取而代之的取而代之的取而代之的取而代之的取而代之的取而代之的取而代之的取而代之的取而代之的取而代之的取而代之.

blocks.en:
The median hides a tail, which the bottom left of Figure 7 reads off directly: 5% of rewrites lose more than 0.25 of the distance to another activation’s account, even though the validated judge calls them meaning-preserving.
Reading the text does not reveal which rewrites these are, so a human monitor could not anticipate them, and this tail is the part of the convention question that remains open.
blocks.zh:
中位数隐藏了尾巴,图7左下方直接读出:5%的重写者损失了超过0.25个与另一个激活账户的距离,尽管经过验证的法官称其为"保留意义".
阅读文本不会显示这些内容的重写,因此人机显示器无法预见,而这一尾巴是公约问题中仍然开放的部分.

blocks.en:
Damage is a ratio of angles, not a proportion of anything countable, so it cannot be read as the percentage of an explanation that is grounded in English.
The map from angle to information is nonlinear, and the denominator is not a true zero, because another conversation’s explanation still shares register and format with the original.
The measure therefore supports comparisons between conditions, as above, rather than absolute statements about how much of the channel is conventional.
blocks.zh:
损害是角度之比,而不是任何可计数的事物之比例,因此不能被解读为基于英语的解释的百分比.
从角度到信息的映射是非线性,分母不是真实的零,因为另一个对话的解释仍然与原作共享注册和格式.
因此,这一措施支持对条件进行比较,如上所述,而不是绝对声明频道的多少是常规的。

blocks.en:
H2 fails: the AR reads plain English written by a model it never trained with nearly as well as its partner’s, and the residual authorship effect is small and measured.
Since rivals are, in addition, 96 to 98% AV-authored, little foreign text is present in them to begin with.
The failure of Experiment #1 is therefore a failure to price truth, not a failure to parse the distractors.
blocks.zh:
H2失败:AR读取了它从未用过近乎于其伙伴的模型所写的平白英语,而残余的作者作用是小而量度的.
由于对手还有96%至98%的AV作者,因此其中很少有外文开始出现.
因此,实验一号的失败是没有给真理定价,而不是没有分析分心者.

Assumption 3.4 is the ELK problem

This is the limitation that most constrains how far the results reach.
Every rival account is false because its content is absent from the conversation, so all our lineups test claims in A input A_{\mathrm{input}} , whose truth the transcript settles.

The finding we can defend is therefore narrower and still informative: the channel discriminates poorly even among claims for which ground truth exists outside the model.
Two observations support this, and neither depends on the restriction.
First, the dissociation between identification and discrimination itself does not depend on which kind of truth is tested, since the same explanations, on the same lineups, identify their activation perfectly and discriminate its true account barely above chance.

blocks.en:
Having separated identification from discrimination (Section 6.2 ), and transcript-level from processing-level accounts (Section 3.4 ), we highlight below precisely where four lines of work on monitoring a model’s internal state stand with respect to the current work.
Each has found that white-box access helps less than hoped wherever the transcript already settles the answer, which is the limitation our own lineups share, and each has built controls for it.
None of them scores a monitor against contrary accounts matched in specificity, which is the measurement that separated identification from discrimination in Section 6.2 .
We take each line of work in turn, and say what our results add to it and what we inherit from it.

在将识别与歧视区分开来(第6.2节),以及记录层与处理层账户区分开来(第3.4节)之后,我们在下文确切地强调了监测模型内部状况的四行工作与当前工作的关系。
每个人发现,白盒访问帮助比希望的少,只要记录本已经解决了答案,这就是我们自己排行份额的限制,并且每个人都为它建立了控制.
其中没有任何一个比对相反的叙述的显示器进行精确的评分,这就是第6.2节中将识别与歧视区分开来的衡量标准。
我们依次进行每一行工作,并说我们的成果增加了多少,我们继承了多少。

blocks.en:
Linear probes trained on simple contrastive data separate deceptive from honest responses of Llama-3.3-70B with AUROC between 0.96 and 0.999 [ 13 ] , but they partly fire on scenarios that are about deception rather than on deception itself, and their authors note that the deception in their datasets is visible in the transcript or chain-of-though of the monitored models. Parrack et al. [28] therefore value a probe by its black-to-white boost, the gain of a monitor that sees probe scores over the same monitor without them.
The boost they find is weak, and it is negative on the one dataset whose veracity the public tokens settle. Kretschmar et al. [16] reach the same conclusion at scale: across seven kinds of lie, every detector fails most where the transcript alone cannot show the lie. Natarajan et al. [27] find that deception detection is heterogeneous though, and that probes matched to a deception type do better. Cooney et al. [9] show that many trained model organisms used as ground truth do not verifiably believe the opposite of what they say.
All of these score a single response as deceptive or not.
Our lineups ask which of several contrary accounts is true, and our experiments in Section 6.2 show the kind of failure a binary score cannot show, since a monitor can be certain that something is wrong while being unable to say which account is right.

First, the measurement of Section 6.2 : the channel identifies activations perfectly while barely discriminating between contrary accounts of them, a dissociation that neither binary detection scores nor agent success rates can show.
Second, our Setting 2 2 (Section 3.4 ) is listener-agnostic, and therefore it provides a single framework to compare different monitors/listeners that would condition on different inputs: any of the monitors above is a listener that scores candidate accounts, so all of them can be compared on identical lineups under Setting 2 2 .
Third, our framework provides the account sets of Section 3 , which say in advance where white-box access can help.
Specifically, a monitor reading X X settles the accounts in A X A_{X} , so it can beat a transcript monitor only on A X ∖ A input A_{X}\setminus A_{\mathrm{input}} .
Our framework is consistent with those previous work as it supports theoretical predictions of the negative results reviewed above: on Backdoors, on lies undecidable from the transcript, on verbaliser benchmarks solvable from text, and on models that explain themselves faithfully.
In return, we inherit the controls these works built, namely the black-to-white comparison, the base-model control, and independent verification of any induced state, and Section 9 leverages them to extend our lineups beyond transcript-level accounts in future works.
